category: Plurals that look exactly like the singular

entries.meaning: The woolly farm animal; figuratively, a person who follows without thinking.
examples: A sheep wandered onto the road.
Forty sheep grazed on the far slope.
These sheep are ready for shearing.
The farm keeps sheep for wool rather than meat.
They follow whatever the ads tell them, like sheep.
He was the black sheep of the family.
That's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

senses.head: The animal
examples: A sheep wandered onto the road.

These sheep are ready for shearing.
The farm keeps sheep for wool rather than meat.

senses.head: A follower, someone easily led
examples: They follow whatever the ads tell them, like sheep.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: He was the black sheep of the family.
That's a wolf in sheep's clothing.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — this sheep is / these sheep are
entries.contrast: ✗ sheeps is always wrong. The meat is mutton and the young animal is a lamb, both separate words. Compare goat, which is perfectly regular: goats.

entries.meaning: The hoofed woodland animal.
examples: A deer crossed in front of the car.

Deer eat everything I plant.

senses.head: The animal
examples: A deer crossed in front of the car.

Deer eat everything I plant.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — a deer was / the deer were
entries.contrast: ✗ deers is wrong. The word once meant any wild animal, which is why it kept the old unmarked plural. Note reindeer and roe deer follow it, but antelope allows both antelope and antelopes.

entries.meaning: The aquatic animal, and its flesh as food.
examples: I caught four fish before lunch.
The fish in this tank are all the same age.
A single fish jumped clear of the water.
The book catalogs the fishes of the Great Lakes.
We're having fish for dinner.
She doesn't eat fish or shellfish.
There are plenty more fish in the sea.
He was a big fish in a small pond.
I felt like a fish out of water at that party.

senses.head: Individual animals
examples: I caught four fish before lunch.
The fish in this tank are all the same age.
A single fish jumped clear of the water.

senses.head: Species or kinds — fishes
body: Biology, and formal or literary writing. (виды рыб)
examples: The book catalogs the fishes of the Great Lakes.

senses.head: As food — uncountable
examples: We're having fish for dinner.
She doesn't eat fish or shellfish.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: There are plenty more fish in the sea.
He was a big fish in a small pond.
I felt like a fish out of water at that party.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the fish is / the fish are
entries.pattern: zero plural, with a marked regular plural for kinds
entries.contrast: The two plurals mean different things. Six fish is six animals; the fishes of the Caribbean is a set of species. As food the word is uncountable: we ate fish, never ✗ we ate a fish unless you mean the whole animal.

entries.meaning: The large northern deer. The American animal; the European one is called an elk.
examples: A moose stood in the middle of the highway.
Two moose were feeding in the shallows.
Moose are far more dangerous than most tourists expect.
We saw a bull moose at dawn.
The park counts its moose by helicopter every winter.

senses.head: The animal
examples: A moose stood in the middle of the highway.
Two moose were feeding in the shallows.
Moose are far more dangerous than most tourists expect.
We saw a bull moose at dawn.
The park counts its moose by helicopter every winter.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — a moose was / the moose were
entries.contrast: ✗ meese is a joke, never a real plural — the word is Algonquian, not Germanic, so the goose → geese pattern cannot touch it. ✗ mooses is also wrong.

entries.meaning: The large deer of North America and northern Eurasia.
examples: A herd of elk moved down into the valley.
We heard an elk bugling before sunrise.
Elk were reintroduced to the region in the 1990s.
The photograph shows a single elk against the snow.
Hunters may take one elk per season.

senses.head: The animal
examples: A herd of elk moved down into the valley.
We heard an elk bugling before sunrise.
Elk were reintroduced to the region in the 1990s.
The photograph shows a single elk against the snow.
Hunters may take one elk per season.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the elk is / the elk are
entries.variants: elk (usual) · elks (less common, and the fraternal order is the Elks)
entries.contrast: The word means different animals on different continents. In North America an elk is the wapiti; in Europe elk is the animal Americans call a moose.

entries.meaning: The large shaggy-shouldered bovine of the North American plains.
examples: A single bison blocked the park road for an hour.

The herd's bison are tagged and tracked.
Bison meat is leaner than beef.

examples: A single bison blocked the park road for an hour.
Thousands of bison once crossed these plains.
The herd's bison are tagged and tracked.
Bison meat is leaner than beef.
She photographed a bison calf beside its mother.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — a bison was / the bison were
entries.contrast: Buffalo is the everyday American word for the same animal and allows three plurals — buffalo, buffaloes, buffalos — while bison allows only one.

entries.meaning: The North American bison, or the water buffalo of Asia and Africa.
examples: A herd of buffalo grazed near the river.
The reserve protects several hundred buffalo.
Water buffaloes pull the plows here.
One buffalo wandered onto the airstrip.
She ordered buffalo wings and a side salad.
Don't let the paperwork buffalo you.

senses.head: The animal
examples: A herd of buffalo grazed near the river.
The reserve protects several hundred buffalo.
Water buffaloes pull the plows here.
One buffalo wandered onto the airstrip.

senses.head: In compounds and place names
examples: She ordered buffalo wings and a side salad.

senses.head: As a verb — to intimidate or bewilder
examples: Don't let the paperwork buffalo you.

entries.plural: buffalo · buffaloes · buffalos — all three accepted
entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the buffalo is / the buffalo are
entries.pattern: zero plural, with two regular alternatives
entries.variants: buffalo is commonest in American usage; buffaloes is the usual written plural elsewhere
entries.contrast: Unusually, all three plurals are correct. American speakers overwhelmingly use the unchanged form for the animal of the plains.

entries.meaning: Pigs collectively, especially as livestock; also a contemptible person.
examples: The outbreak spread quickly among the swine.
Swine were kept behind the barn.
The disease is named swine flu for a reason.
That swine left without paying.
The pair of them are absolute swines.
Don't cast pearls before swine.

senses.head: The animals
examples: The outbreak spread quickly among the swine.
Swine were kept behind the barn.
The disease is named swine flu for a reason.

senses.head: A contemptible person
body: Chiefly British in flavor but understood everywhere. (свинья, подлец)
examples: That swine left without paying.
The pair of them are absolute swines.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: Don't cast pearls before swine.

entries.plural: swine — unchanged · swines in the insult sense
entries.agreement: plural verb — swine are susceptible to the virus
entries.variants: swine (animals, formal or veterinary) · swines (occasionally, of people)
entries.contrast: The ordinary American word for the animal is pig or hog; swine survives in farming, veterinary, and biblical contexts, and as an insult.

entries.meaning: The pink-fleshed migratory fish, and its flesh as food.
examples: A salmon leapt at the base of the falls.
Thousands of salmon return to this river each fall.
The salmon were running early that year.
We had grilled salmon and rice.
Smoked salmon is the one thing he'll always eat.
She wore a salmon pink dress.

senses.head: The fish
examples: A salmon leapt at the base of the falls.
Thousands of salmon return to this river each fall.
The salmon were running early that year.

senses.head: As food — uncountable
examples: We had grilled salmon and rice.
Smoked salmon is the one thing he'll always eat.

senses.head: As a color
examples: She wore a salmon pink dress.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the salmon is / the salmon are
entries.contrast: The l is never pronounced — /ˈsæmən/, not ✗ /ˈsælmən/. Same silent l as in almond for many speakers, and in calm and palm.

entries.meaning: The freshwater game fish.
examples: He caught six trout before noon.
The stream is stocked with trout every spring.
A large trout rose to the fly.
These trout are all hatchery fish.
We ate trout cooked over the fire.

senses.head: The fish
examples: He caught six trout before noon.

A large trout rose to the fly.
These trout are all hatchery fish.

senses.head: As food
examples: We ate trout cooked over the fire.

entries.plural: trout — unchanged · trouts rarely, for species
entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the trout is / the trout are
entries.contrast: Like fish, the marked plural trouts appears only when distinguishing kinds, and even then most writers prefer trout species.

entries.meaning: The cold-water food fish of the North Atlantic.
examples: The boats brought in three hundred cod.
A single cod can weigh forty pounds.

senses.head: The fish
examples: The boats brought in three hundred cod.
A single cod can weigh forty pounds.
Cod have been fished here for five centuries.

senses.head: As food
examples: Fried cod is on the menu every Friday.
She ordered the cod with potatoes.

entries.plural: cod — unchanged · cods rarely, for species
entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the cod is / the cod are
entries.contrast: Compare haddock, mackerel, and herring, which behave the same way. Fish names are the most productive corner of the zero-plural pattern.

entries.meaning: The small edible crustacean; informally, a very small person.
examples: We ordered a pound of shrimp.
The shrimp were still frozen solid.

senses.head: The animal, and the food

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the shrimp is / the shrimp are

entries.contrast: Shrimps is not wrong but sounds foreign to American ears. In the 'small person' sense the plural is always regular: shrimps.

entries.meaning: The ten-armed marine mollusk, and its flesh as food.
examples: The boat landed two tons of squid.

entries.meaning: The plump game bird of moors and northern forests.
examples: A grouse burst out of the heather.
They shot four grouse that afternoon.
Grouse nest directly on the ground.

She groused all the way home.

senses.head: The bird
examples: A grouse burst out of the heather.
They shot four grouse that afternoon.
Grouse nest directly on the ground.

senses.head: As a verb — to grumble
examples: He grouses about the weather every single morning.
She groused all the way home.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the grouse is / the grouse are
entries.contrast: Despite rhyming with mouse and louse, this bird never becomes ✗ grice. It is also a verb meaning 'to complain', and that verb is perfectly regular: grouses, groused, grousing.

senses.head: The bird
examples: A covey of quail scattered into the brush.
We roasted two quail for dinner.
Quail are common along the fence lines here.
She spotted a single quail on the path.

senses.head: As a verb — to flinch
examples: He quailed under the judge's stare.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the quail is / the quail are
entries.pattern: zero plural, with a regular alternative

entries.meaning: A number of things or events coming one after another; a set of related broadcasts or publications.
examples: A series of small errors caused the outage.
This series of lectures is open to the public.
She published a series of essays on the subject.
The series was canceled after two seasons.
Both series are streaming now.
He's read every book in the series.
The series goes to whoever wins tonight.

senses.head: A sequence of related things or events
body: Takes a singular verb when the sequence is treated as one unit. (серия, ряд)
examples: A series of small errors caused the outage.
This series of lectures is open to the public.
She published a series of essays on the subject.

senses.head: A set of television programs or books
examples: The series was canceled after two seasons.
Both series are streaming now.
He's read every book in the series.

senses.head: In sports — a set of games between the same teams
examples: The series goes to whoever wins tonight.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — this series is / these series are
entries.pattern: invariable, the -s is part of the stem
entries.contrast: The -s is not a plural ending — it belongs to the Latin stem. So a single one is a series, never ✗ a serie, and several are still series. The verb tells you which: a series of talks is planned versus both series are sold out.

entries.meaning: A group of organisms capable of interbreeding; more loosely, a kind or type.
examples: This species is found only on one island.

The species has been extinct since the 1930s.
Several species of oak grow in the park.
It is a species of argument that convinces nobody.

senses.head: A biological kind
examples: This species is found only on one island.
Over two hundred species were recorded in the survey.
The species has been extinct since the 1930s.
Several species of oak grow in the park.

senses.head: A type or sort, figuratively
examples: It is a species of argument that convinces nobody.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — this species is / these species are
entries.pattern: invariable, the -s is part of the stem
entries.contrast: ✗ a specie is wrong — specie is a separate word meaning coined money. The singular is a species, with the -s.

entries.meaning: A machine capable of flight.
examples: The aircraft landed safely on one engine.
Six aircraft were parked on the apron.
All aircraft are grounded until the storm passes.

Two aircraft were reported missing.

senses.head: A flying machine
examples: The aircraft landed safely on one engine.
Six aircraft were parked on the apron.
All aircraft are grounded until the storm passes.

Two aircraft were reported missing.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the aircraft is / the aircraft are
entries.contrast: ✗ aircrafts is wrong. Every -craft compound behaves the same way: spacecraft, watercraft, hovercraft. The standalone noun craft meaning 'a skill' is different and takes a regular plural: traditional crafts.

entries.meaning: A skill or trade; also a boat or other vessel.
examples: Weaving is a craft that takes years to learn.

senses.head: A skill or handmade trade
examples: Weaving is a craft that takes years to learn.
The fair features traditional crafts from the region.
She takes her craft seriously.

senses.head: A vessel — boat or aircraft
examples: Small craft were advised to stay in port.
A single craft approached the dock.

senses.head: Cunning, skill in deceiving
body: Uncountable, and the source of crafty. (хитрость)
examples: He got the contract by pure craft.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the craft is / the craft are
entries.pattern: regular in one sense, zero plural in the other
entries.variants: crafts (a skill or trade) · craft (a vessel)
entries.contrast: Two senses, two plurals. Skills and handmade trades are crafts; boats and flying machines are craft, unchanged. Small craft warnings means several boats, not several skills.

entries.meaning: The young of a person, animal, or plant.
examples: The pair produced four offspring in three years.

Their offspring are marked and released.
He arrived with his three offspring in tow.

The company is the offspring of two failed startups.

senses.head: The young of an animal
examples: The pair produced four offspring in three years.
A single offspring survived the winter.
Their offspring are marked and released.

senses.head: Someone's children
examples: He arrived with his three offspring in tow.
The estate passed to her offspring.

senses.head: Something produced by something else
examples: The company is the offspring of two failed startups.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — the offspring is / the offspring are
entries.contrast: ✗ offsprings is wrong. The word covers any number, and about people it is either formal-scientific or jokey — ordinary speech says children.

entries.meaning: A method or instrument for achieving something; also, financial resources.
examples: Email is the fastest means of reaching her.
Every means was tried before they gave up.
All means of escape were blocked.
It was simply a means to an end.
They live well beyond their means.
A family of modest means paid for the whole thing.
By all means, take the last one.
By no means is this settled.

senses.head: A method or way
body: Singular and plural identical; the article and verb disambiguate. (средство, способ)
examples: Email is the fastest means of reaching her.
Every means was tried before they gave up.
All means of escape were blocked.
It was simply a means to an end.

senses.head: Financial resources
examples: They live well beyond their means.
A family of modest means paid for the whole thing.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: By all means, take the last one.
By no means is this settled.

entries.agreement: depends on meaning — one means is / several means are
entries.pattern: invariable, the -s is part of the stem
entries.contrast: ✗ a mean is wrong in this sense — a mean is a mathematical average. Singular and plural are both means: a means to an end, all available means. The separate sense 'money, resources' is always plural.

entries.meaning: The main office or command center of an organization.
examples: The company's headquarters is in Denver.
Both headquarters were evacuated.
They moved headquarters twice in five years.
Police headquarters has issued a statement.
Orders came down from headquarters that morning.

senses.head: The main office of an organization
examples: The company's headquarters is in Denver.
Both headquarters were evacuated.
They moved headquarters twice in five years.
Police headquarters has issued a statement.

senses.head: A military command center
examples: Orders came down from headquarters that morning.

entries.agreement: either — the headquarters is (the building) / are (the people)
entries.contrast: ✗ a headquarter does not exist as a noun. One organization has a headquarters, and two organizations have two headquarters. American usage leans toward a singular verb when the building is meant.

entries.meaning: A building or group of buildings housing soldiers.
examples: The new barracks was finished in the spring.

He shared a barracks with forty other men.

entries.agreement: either — the barracks is / are
entries.contrast: ✗ a barrack is rare and sounds wrong to American ears. One building is a barracks; several are barracks.

entries.meaning: A place where roads meet; figuratively, a point of decision.
examples: Turn left at the crossroads.
The village grew up around a crossroads.
Two crossroads farther on, you'll see the sign.

senses.head: A road junction
examples: Turn left at the crossroads.
The village grew up around a crossroads.
Two crossroads farther on, you'll see the sign.

senses.head: A decisive moment
body: Figurative, and very common. (распутье, переломный момент)
examples: The company is at a crossroads.
She found herself at a crossroads after graduation.
We stand at a crossroads in this negotiation.

entries.agreement: usually singular — a crossroads is
entries.contrast: ✗ a crossroad exists but is much rarer; the standard singular keeps the -s. The figurative sense is nearly always singular: at a crossroads.

entries.meaning: A branch of the military, or an organized body of people with a shared function.
examples: He served in the Marine Corps for eight years.

senses.head: A military formation or branch
examples: He served in the Marine Corps for eight years.
Two corps advanced along the river.
The Army Corps of Engineers built the levee.

senses.head: An organized group with a common activity
examples: The press corps filed into the briefing room.
She joined the Peace Corps after college.
The diplomatic corps was invited to the reception.

entries.pronunciation note: the ps is silent, like core
entries.plural: corps /kɔːrz/ · korz — spelled the same, pronounced with a /z/
entries.agreement: either — the corps is / are
entries.pattern: invariable in spelling, distinguished only in sound
entries.contrast: The trap is the pronunciation. Never say ✗ /kɔːrps/ — the p and s are both silent in the singular, so it sounds exactly like core. In the plural you add only a /z/. Do not confuse it with corpse /kɔːrps/, a dead body, where the p is pronounced.

entries.meaning: A group of twelve.
examples: We need three dozen eggs for the recipe.
She bought two dozen roses.
A half dozen people were waiting.
Dozens of complaints arrived that week.
He has dozens of excuses and none of them work.
Cheap sunglasses are a dime a dozen around here.
We talked nineteen to the dozen the whole drive.

senses.head: After a specific number — unchanged, no of
examples: We need three dozen eggs for the recipe.
She bought two dozen roses.
A half dozen people were waiting.

senses.head: Without a number — plural, with of
examples: Dozens of complaints arrived that week.
He has dozens of excuses and none of them work.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: Cheap sunglasses are a dime a dozen around here.
We talked nineteen to the dozen the whole drive.

entries.plural: dozen after a number · dozens when vague
entries.agreement: plural verb — two dozen eggs are enough
entries.contrast: The rule is exact and catches everyone. After a specific number, no -s and no of: three dozen eggs. Without a number, add both: dozens of eggs. The same rule governs hundred, thousand, million, and score.

entries.meaning: The number 100.
examples: Two hundred people attended.
The repair cost five hundred dollars.
It's about three hundred miles from here.
Hundreds of birds settled on the water.
She has read hundreds of these applications.
I'm feeling a hundred percent better today.
The odds were a hundred to one.

senses.head: After a specific number — unchanged, no of
examples: Two hundred people attended.
The repair cost five hundred dollars.
It's about three hundred miles from here.

senses.head: Without a number — plural, with of
examples: Hundreds of birds settled on the water.
She has read hundreds of these applications.

senses.head: In fixed expressions
examples: I'm feeling a hundred percent better today.
The odds were a hundred to one.

entries.plural: hundred after a number · hundreds when vague
entries.agreement: plural verb — two hundred people were there
entries.contrast: Identical to dozen: ✗ two hundreds people and ✗ hundred of people are both wrong. Say two hundred people or hundreds of people. Thousand, million, and billion follow the same rule.

Haddock are smaller than cod.

She ordered the haddock and chips.

entries.meaning: The freshwater food fish.
examples: We caught a dozen perch off the dock.
